# Up Anyway: every brave idea, Oops Mission and goat line

Every built-in idea card she can pick and everything the goat says, in one place, grouped the way they come up in the game and written the way she sees them.

- 49 brave ideas in 5 groups
- 22 Oops Missions
- 286 goat lines in 45 groups

**This file is generated from the game’s content. Don’t edit it by hand.**

- To change the words, edit `src/content/ideas.ts` (brave ideas and Oops Missions) or `src/content/goatLines.ts` (everything the goat says), then run `npm run review` to rebuild this file.
- The layout (the groups, their order and the notes on when the goat says each line) lives in `tests/unit/review.test.ts`.
- `npx vitest run` fails while this file is out of date, so it always matches the game.

**Hiding a card:** Grown-ups → Idea cards → Built-in idea cards lists the same cards in the same groups and order, each with a Shown/Hidden switch. A hidden card is never deleted and can be shown again any time. The small code after each card here is its id.

## 1. Brave ideas (49)

Her “Pick an idea” screen (from Log a brave thing), in its groups and order. It always starts with this line:

> **Brave means safe but scary.** If something could really hurt you or someone else, the brave move is to stop and tell a grown-up.

Cards a grown-up adds in parent mode show under “Extra ideas”, just before the Oops Missions. They are saved on the device, so they aren’t listed here.

## 3. The goat’s lines (286)

The goat rides in her backpack and is scared of heights: it is the fear, coming along and saying so out loud while the climb goes on anyway. Within a group the goat goes through every line before any comes round again, and never says the same line twice in a row.

How to read the notes:

- **{n}**, **{pose}** and the other words in curly brackets are filled in when the line is said; each group says what with. A line is skipped when there’s nothing to fill it with, so the {n} lines only come up once the count is 2 or more.
- *(moral)*: one of the few gentle morals. Only at a camp, and at most one per camp visit.
- *(only while the goat is in the backpack)*: skipped once the goat is out of the backpack, on night climbs and at camp after Sky Lake.
- *(only on night climbs …)* and *(only after Sky Lake …)*: said only once the goat is out of the backpack.
- *(only in Gusty Ridge)* and the like: only in that part of the mountain. *(only when the rope catches her)* and the like: only for that kind of fall.

### 3.1 First run (5 lines)

Setup, once a grown-up has handed it over.

#### Meeting the goat (3)

*When:* After she designs her climber, the goat peeks out of the backpack. She taps Next between the lines.

- Oh! Hello. I’m a baby mountain goat.
- Funny thing about me: I’m scared of heights.
- But I want to see the top. Can I come anyway?

#### Naming the goat (1)

*When:* She has just typed a name for the goat.

*Filled in:* {goat} is the name she gave it.

- {goat}? I love it!

#### Naming her mountain (1)

*When:* On the screen where she names her mountain.

- Whoa, that’s tall. My knees are wobbling already.

### 3.2 The lesson (6 lines)

The short lesson at the end of setup: one leap up to a ledge, then fall practice.

#### Learning to leap (3)

*When:* The lesson starts with the first line. If she waits 6 seconds without leaping, the goat says one of the others.

- Drag back, then let go. That’s how we leap! *(said first)*
- Pull back like a slingshot, then let go!
- Drag back, let go, and I’ll hold on tight!

#### The first leap lands (1)

*When:* Her first leap in the lesson lands on the ledge.

- Our first leap! My tummy’s still down there.

#### Fall practice (1)

*When:* Two seconds later: fall practice, from a spot where every leap ends on the rope.

- Now we practise falling. Gulp. Leap anywhere you like!

#### The rope’s first catch (1)

*When:* The first time the rope ever catches her (the lesson’s fall practice). It says why the rope is there.

- The rope catches us. That’s why climbers can try hard moves!

### 3.3 The end of setup (2 lines)

#### Brave versus dangerous (1)

*When:* The setup screen that says brave means safe but scary, and that if something could really hurt her or someone else, the brave move is to stop and tell a grown-up.

- Like me in your backpack: scared, but safe.

#### Off to Pitch 1 (1)

*When:* The last setup screen, just before Pitch 1.

- My knees are knocking. Let’s go up anyway?

#### Offering beta (4)

*When:* After 3 falls at one spot, as the hint button appears. Hints are free.

- Want some beta? Climbers share tips all the time.

- Asking for beta is what real climbers do. Tip?
- Want my idea? Climbers swap ideas all day long.

#### Beta hints (29)

*When:* She taps the hint button. The goat looks at how her last leap from that spot missed and says a line from the matching group.

Too short:

- We were a bit short. More power?
- Didn’t quite reach! Pull back further?
- Our chalk stops before it. More oomph?
- A longer drag might get us there. Want to try?
- Just short! Drag back a bit more?

Too far:

- We flew right past it! A bit less pull?
- Too much zoom! Try a shorter drag?
- Whoosh, right over it! Gentler this time?
- We had loads of power. Maybe a bit less?

Too steep (lots of up, not much across):

- Lots of up, not much across. Aim more sideways?
- We went up like a rocket! Lean the aim over?
- Too high, not far enough. Aim a little lower?
- We popped straight up. Tip the aim toward it?

Too flat:

- We went too flat. Aim a bit higher?
- Not enough up! Point it more at the sky?
- We skimmed along low. Try a taller arc?
- A higher arc, maybe? Ours was a bit flat.

Bumped into a ledge on the way:

- We bonked a ledge on the way. Different angle?
- Bonk! Something got in the way. Try a new arc?
- A ledge bumped us. Can we arc around it?
- Bump! Shall we find an arc that misses that ledge?

Pushed by a gust:

- The wind shoved us! Wait for it to calm?
- Watch the grass. Leap when it’s still?
- A gust got us. Leap between the whooshes?
- The wind has a rhythm. Leap in the quiet bit?

The ledge crumbled under her:

- That ledge crumbles. Leap off a bit quicker?
- Crumbly ledge! Aim fast and go?
- It crumbled under us. Hop off sooner next time?
- Crumbly ones don’t wait. Shall we leap sooner?

### 3.5 Looks Scary (30 lines)

One moment in each of the first five zones, on the middle pitch: something looks scary from below and turns out gentle up close. Before it, she gives a Fear Forecast; after it, she’s asked “How scary was it really?”. The first time she meets each one, the goat only says that moment’s own lines.

#### The huge gap: Meadow Slopes, Pitch 2 (4)

*When:* The first Big Leap looks like a huge gap above a misty drop. Up close, it’s an easy hop.

Before, as it comes into view:

- That gap looks HUGE. My knees are melting.
- Is that a gap or a canyon? Gulp.

After, up close:

- That giant gap? Just a big hop! My knees still wobbled, though.
- Up close, the giant gap was just a big step!

#### Glowing eyes: Firefly Hollow, Pitch 5 (4)

*When:* Glowing eyes in a dark cave. They’re fireflies.

Before, as it comes into view:

- Glowing eyes in the cave! Lots of them!
- Something in that cave is looking at us. Eek.

After, up close:

- The eyes were fireflies! Hello, tiny lights!
- Fireflies! Not eyes at all. They’re blinking hello!

#### The rumbling cliff: Crumble Cliffs, Pitch 8 (4)

*When:* The whole cliff rumbles and growls. It’s a bear, snoring in its cave.

Before, as it comes into view:

- The whole cliff is rumbling! What IS that?
- Grrrumble. Did the mountain just growl at us?

After, up close:

- It was just a sleepy bear, snoring! Shh, tiptoe.
- The rumble was a bear, snoring! A sleepy, cozy bear.

#### The rickety rope bridge: Gusty Ridge, Pitch 11 (4)

*When:* A wobbly, creaking rope bridge. It holds.

Before, as it comes into view:

- A wobbly rope bridge. Wobblier than my knees!
- That bridge creaks. My hooves are not happy.

After, up close:

- The bridge held! Wobbly, and totally fine.
- It creaked and swayed, and it held us up!

#### The giant shadow: Cloud Steps, Pitch 14 (4)

*When:* A giant shadow in the fog. It’s a fluffy marmot with the sun behind it.

Before, as it comes into view:

- A GIANT shadow in the fog! How big is it?
- Something enormous is up there. I can see its ears!

After, up close:

- The giant was a fluffy marmot! Fluffier than me!
- The giant shadow? A marmot, sunbathing! So fluffy.

#### Any of the five, on later climbs (10)

*When:* Climbing past a moment she has met before, the goat may also say one of these.

Before, as it comes into view:

- What IS that? It looks super scary.
- My ears are hiding. That thing looks scary.
- That looks SO scary. Let’s go and see anyway?
- Gulp. How scary does that look to you?
- I’m scared of that. Let’s get close and find out.

After, up close:

- Huh. Looked way scarier from down there.
- Up close it’s… kind of nice?
- My scary guess was way bigger than the real thing.
- Scary from far away. Cozy up close. Huh!
- We went anyway. It’s nothing like I imagined!

### 3.6 Camp (65 lines)

At camp and the screens around it: logging a brave thing, the cairn and Plans.

#### The first visit to camp (1)

*When:* Her very first visit to camp: the goat points out where they’re going.

- See the very top? That’s Sky Lake. That’s where we’re going.

#### Sitting at camp (23)

*When:* One line each visit to camp, and another each time she taps the picture. At most one moral per visit.

- The fire’s warm. My legs have nearly stopped wobbling.
- I like camp. The ground stays exactly where it is.
- The mountain looks very tall today. Let’s go anyway?
- My hooves are ready. My tummy is still deciding.
- Your backpack is the comfiest spot on the whole mountain. *(only while the goat is in the backpack)*
- I peeked up the trail. Still high. Still coming.
- Sitting by the fire is my best skill.
- Somewhere up there is Sky Lake. I wonder if it’s splashy. *(only while the goat is in the backpack)*
- The fire crackled. I jumped. I’m still sitting here, though.
- Want to hear my fierce noise? Meh-eh-eh. Terrifying.
- Somebody’s tummy rumbled. Not mine. Okay, mine.
- Mountain goats are meant to love heights. I’m a special one.
- I counted the stars last night. I got to eleven.
- I dreamed we could see the whole world from Sky Lake. *(only while the goat is in the backpack)*
- I still have Sky Lake in my ears. Best flop ever. *(only after Sky Lake, with the goat out beside her)*
- Out of the backpack, by the fire. Still a bit wobbly. *(only after Sky Lake, with the goat out beside her)*
- We saw everything from the top. My knees still remember. *(only after Sky Lake, with the goat out beside her)*
- Climb by moonlight sometime? I’ll bring my wobbly legs. *(only after Sky Lake, with the goat out beside her)*
- Being scared just means it matters to us. *(moral)*
- You don’t have to stop being scared to go. *(moral)*
- I’m scared lots. I come anyway. That’s my whole trick. *(moral)*
- Every flop teaches us something. Even the silly ones. *(moral)*
- Scared legs can still climb. Mine do it every day. *(moral)*

#### Saving a plan (5)

*When:* Logging a brave thing, she chose “I’ll do it later”: it goes to her Plans, and the goat greets it there.

- Saved for later! I’ll keep it safe in the backpack. *(only while the goat is in the backpack)*
- A plan! It can wait as long as it likes.
- Later is a real time. It’ll be right here.
- Into Plans it goes. My knees say thank you.
- Whenever you’re ready, so is this plan.

#### A brave thing that flopped (7)

*When:* Logging a brave thing she has done, she chose “Flopped — and I’m still here”. Said with respect, never as a joke.

- It didn’t go how you hoped. You still did it.
- Flopped, and still here. That’s the bravest kind.
- You tried something really scary. A flop doesn’t undo that.
- Thank you for telling me. Flops are hard to say.
- Here’s a hoof hug. You went anyway.
- The scary part was going. You did that part.
- I’ve had real flops too. I’m still here, like you.

#### A stone lands on the cairn (11)

*When:* A new stone lands on her cairn. The goat never mentions her fear numbers or how it went.

*Filled in:* {thing} is the first few words of the brave thing (lines with it are skipped for a letter’s stone); {n} is how many stones the cairn holds now.

- Clack! “{thing}” is on the cairn now.
- You did “{thing}”! The cairn got taller.
- “{thing}”: you really did that one.
- “{thing}” is a stone now. Clack!
- A stone for “{thing}”! I heard it land.
- Clack! Stone {n}. Each one is something real you did.
- Clack! A real-life stone. Those are my favourite kind.
- A new stone! I heard that clack from the backpack. *(only while the goat is in the backpack)*
- That stone is yours forever. Nobody can take it off.
- Our cairn’s getting taller than me!
- “{thing}”! The mountain heard that clack, I’m sure.

#### The cairn is full for today (2)

*When:* A new stone is over the day’s limit of three, so it waits beside the cairn.

- The cairn’s full for today. This stone goes on tomorrow. *(when it goes on tomorrow)*
- The cairn’s full for today. This stone waits its turn. *(when other stones are already waiting ahead of it)*

#### Visiting the cairn (5)

*When:* She opens the cairn and no new stone is arriving.

- These stones are all real things you did.
- I like sitting by our cairn. It feels like a hug.
- Tap a stone and I’ll listen to its story again.
- Wobbly ones, flopped ones, nailed ones: all here together.
- I gave our cairn a sniff. It smells like real life.

#### The empty cairn (2)

*When:* She opens the cairn before her first stone.

- This hilltop is saving a spot for our first stone.
- One real brave thing, and a stone lands right here.

#### Not today (5)

*When:* She taps “Not today” on a plan. It costs nothing. The first line is always said; a few seconds later, one of the others.

- Fear won this round. That’s allowed. *(always said first)*
- Not today is a real answer. The plan will keep.
- My tummy said no too. Some days are like that.
- Okay! It’ll still be here whenever you want it.
- No rush. Mountains are very good at waiting.

#### Make it smaller (4)

*When:* She taps “Make it smaller” on a plan and picks a smaller step (half of it, with someone first, practise at home first, or her own).

- A smaller step still goes up. I love small steps.
- Tiny steps! I climb everything in tiny steps.
- Half of it still makes my knees wobble. I’m in!
- A smaller step! My knees like this plan already.

### 3.7 Sky Lake (9 lines)

The top of the mountain.

#### The Sky Lake finale (4)

*When:* Her first send of the summit pitch, in this order.

- Sky Lake! We made it. I can see EVERYTHING. *(arriving at Sky Lake)*
- My turn. My legs are jelly. I’m going anyway! *(before the goat’s own wobbly leap)*
- SPLASH! I flopped right in! Best flop ever! *(the splash)*
- We were scared the whole way up. And we came anyway. *(on the closing card)*

#### The night ending (1)

*When:* Sending the summit pitch on a night climb (after Sky Lake): a short ending where they both splash in.

- Both of us this time! One, two, three… SPLASH!

#### Remembering Sky Lake (4)

*When:* At camp after Sky Lake, on the first visit of each day.

*Filled in:* {mountain} is the name she gave her mountain.

- We climbed all of {mountain}! I’m still a bit dizzy!
- We went all the way up, and every flop came too.
- I was scared at every single step. Best climb ever.
- Sky Lake was so splashy. My ears are still wet!
